security_spec.violation_condition: When XiangShan trace encoder parameter return_stack_size_p > 0, the irdepth field width is computed as return_stack_size_p + call_counter_size_p (old formula) instead of return_stack_size_p + 1 + call_counter_size_p (new formula). This occurs when the Chisel/Verilog hardware trace packet generator instantiates the irdepth field width as a compile-time Wire or Reg parameter using the uncorrected expression, causing the field to be 1 bit too narrow in Format 0/1/2 packets. The bit-level packet serializer then shifts subsequent fields (irreport or padding) into the bit position that should belong to irdepth[MSB], corrupting the entire packet bitstream alignment for any downstream trace decoder.
security_spec.summary: irdepth field bit-width miscalculation omits required +1 term when return_stack_size_p > 0, causing trace encoder to generate malformed packets with truncated stack-depth/call-count values, corrupting program-flow reconstruction for all trace consumers

findings.finding: The XiangShan repository only defines the core-side trace source interface (TraceCoreInterface). The XSTOP trace encoder that performs E-Trace packetization — including the irdepth field whose width is computed from return_stack_size_p and call_counter_size_p — is an external IP block integrated via XSTopPrefix. No irdepth, return_stack_size_p, call_counter_size_p, or packet format logic exists in this repository or any of its 10 submodules.

The Trace module is a 4-stage pipeline (s0: ROB commit info, s1: register, s2: TraceBuffer compress, s3: output to encoder) that produces raw trace groups. It does NOT perform E-Trace packet generation, irdepth field computation, or any packet format serialization. Those functions reside in the external XSTOP encoder.

The TraceBuffer compresses per-cycle ROB commit info into trace groups and feeds them to the external encoder. It implements a circular queue with enq/deq pointers and backpressure (blockCommit). No packet format logic, irdepth computation, or XSTOP encoder internals are present here.

The XiangShan trace parameters define only group count, address width, itype width, and ilastsize width. No XSTOP encoder parameters (return_stack_size_p, call_counter_size_p, irdepth) or packet format configuration exist in the parameter definitions.
findings.snippet:
val traceParams: TraceParams = new TraceParams(
    TraceGroupNum  = 3,
    IaddrWidth     = GPAddrBitsSv48x4,
    PrivWidth      = 3,
    ItypeWidth     = 4,
    IlastsizeWidth = 1,
  )

findings.finding: Top-level trace wiring flattens the core's trace group outputs into flat bit vectors (valid, iaddr, itype, iretire, ilastsize) for the external XSTOP encoder. This is the integration boundary — no packet format logic resides here. The XSTOP encoder module itself is not instantiated in XiangShan RTL; it is linked externally at build time via XSTopPrefix.
